accepted_edits.reason: the s31 Why and done-when edits are exactly what findings done_when-1 and reasoning-1 of r-20261116T112049598893 asked for, and the s30 declaration is what wiring-1 asked for

findings.reason: the declaration is the only thing a dispatcher reads to decide what is still to build, so leaving a landed section queued either re-runs it or collides with s31's edits to the same module.
findings.text: `plan-section-declarations` declares s30 `implementable`, while s31's Why (plan.html:416) states "After §30 landed at f47935d07b", and the committed commit f47935d07b is an ancestor of the snapshot base; the plan therefore contradicts its own record file, and a dispatch that reads the declarations queues a landed section again on the same source path (`reckon/run_store.py`) s31 also edits

findings.reason: one number in the section makes the comparison arm falsifiable; without it the node can set the threshold to whatever its base run already satisfies.
findings.text: the first arm is "a read of one plan's runs holds the store for no longer than a read of a single run by id, within a stated factor the test fixes", which names no factor, so the tolerance is the node's to choose; a factor large enough to admit the base behaviour makes the arm hold before the fix too, and the arm then measures nothing while the node still reports a red-at-base pair

findings.reason: a node that fixes plan-filtered selection can pass every arm of s31 and leave the fleet-wide activity-window scan still holding the lock, which is the observed `database is locked` refusal the section exists to remove.
findings.text: the Why says `compose_owed_plan_reviews` "reads one plan's authoring runs through a plan-scoped `stored_run_rows`, and that query selects by plan", but that pass reads the store through `plan_authoring_runs` with `ledger.read_records(project, with_figures=False, activity_since=moment - PLAN_REVIEW_BURST_SECONDS)` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4035-4039) and passes no plan, so `_record_rows` (reckon/run_store.py:293-300) installs `record_epoch` over four extracted stamps per row, not `record_plan` over `json.loads(payload)`; the per-row Python work inside the one statement is the same defect class, but the selection it names is not the read the station holds, and s31's whole measure is scoped to the plan-filtered read
